SetupValue.description: One effective setting; `value` is absent when nothing chooses one.

ShellTab.description: A retained shell identity, independent of its tool pane and current selection.

ShipMark.description: When someone approved or stopped Auto-Ship, and who.

ShippingSnapshot.description:
What a shipping Task is doing, derived from its ship process, its state
and its landing. Nothing here waits on a person.

reason.description: One line saying what is happening.

shipped_at.description: When the Task was handed off.

SlotLayout.description:
A Dashboard page's fixed slots. Members fill slots by number, in order, and
overflow to further pages; they never add, remove or resize slots.

authors.description: Recorded steer authors. Empty for every other source.

count.description: Assets, steers, tool results or compactions; unknown when unrecorded.

SplitAxis.description: `vertical` places children side by side; `horizontal` stacks them.

Starter.description:
Who started a Process, derived from its ancestry: the first Session an
agent ran it from, else the person at the root of its chain.

oneOf.description:
A person ran it. `name` is absent when no participant is configured or
the chain is missing rows: attribution unresolved.
An agent in this Session ran it, for its person.

assembled_tokens.description: Everything Loopflow assembled and submitted, in cl100k tokens.

first_request_tokens.description: Input the provider reported for its first and largest requests.

answers.description: The newest request this reading began after.

unavailable.description: Why the read failed. `body` is then `null`.

oneOf.description: `preview`: the strategy a sync would take; nothing moved.
The sync runs detached as `process`, with its output in `log`.
The sync, continue or abort finished in place.

fork_base.description: The recorded stack base shared by planning, integration and the PR range.

head.description: The commit the plan classified; the sync refuses if HEAD moved since.

linear_id.description: Optional Linear binding, not a second owner of this record.

pm_snapshot_synced_at.description: Acquisition time of the retained Linear observation, never a write clock.

rank.description: Shared planning fields; independent of local execution and Workflow position.

repo_id.description: Stable repository identity, independent of planning membership.

revision.description: Local optimistic-write revision; independent of Linear observation age.

state.description: Linear's state type, `completed` once done; the lifecycle is `TaskState`.

wave_id.description: Read projection from the Project join, validated against the Project on save.

TaskAcquisition.description: Acquisition evidence is independent of saved Work and outbound delivery.

TaskComments.description:
The saved Task thread, its pending deliveries and any failed refresh.
Partial provider reads never replace the retained thread.

conflicts.description: Losing local comment bodies; the thread contains the adopted Linear values.

TaskConditionSnapshot.description: A Task's shared condition and the evidence that proves it.

evidence_age_secs.description: Age of the durable Work evidence at that sample, if Work exists.

observed_at.description: RFC3339 time local workspace evidence was sampled.

unresolved_execution.description:
Started work a finished plan has not settled: the Task is still ready,
its Graph is not idle, or its checkout holds observed unsettled work.
Keeps a terminal Task in the working set.

TaskConditionState.description:
A Task's derived operating condition. Sessions own review actions; this state
only lets Work surfaces explain whether the Task is clear, waiting on
another actor, blocked, or unreadable.

TaskCreateOutcome.description:
A recoverable create/start result. In-progress and uncertain outcomes never
authorize another Graph run; clients keep the same request ID and Task ID.

TaskCreateReceipt.description:
What `lf task create --run --json` prints whenever the Task was filed: the
Task, the graph it took up and the conversation to open. A headless (`-b`)
caller opens no conversation; a run that failed leaves both absent and the
command still exits non-zero, so callers never file the request twice.

oneOf.description: Historical authored direction; the immutable publication owns its text.

A request to end the Task's current turn so the next one re-reads its
direction immediately. A live run acts on interrupts issued after it
launched; there is nothing to interrupt otherwise. Not a report out.

captured.description: The Session input that step captured, when it opened one.

step.description: Label of the latest Graph's latest step, while that Graph is unfinished.

oneOf.description: Its step is waiting out a usage limit until an account frees up.

TaskFollowUp.description: Historical keep-open scope, retained for event decoding only.

TaskGraph.description: One Task's Graph as `lf task status --json` carries it.

oneOf.description:
The Task stands at `start`, at `end`, or at this interactive step,
waiting on a person in the Task conversation.

`lf task run` (`lf_process_id`) carries the Task on from `step`.
`running` is read from that Process: a run that ended without
arriving stopped, and the next `lf task run` starts it again.

TaskOverview.description: Workspace facts needed before opening diagnostic Process history.

TaskOwnership.description:
This Machine's reading of a Task's ownership. `superseded_by` names a later
claim that every other Machine follows while this Machine keeps its own.

TaskOwnershipEntry.description:
One immutable entry in a Task's ownership log. `machine_id` names the
claimant, the handoff target, or the unclaiming Machine.

machine_label.description: The Machine's label when written, or as best known on this Machine.

person_key.description: The person's stable key; names are display only.

ci_observation.description:
The most recent required-check reading for this PR's open head. `None`
until the head has been observed; ignored once the head moves past
`CiObservation::head_sha`.

github_observation.description:
Last GitHub refresh attempt. A fresh result coalesces reads briefly; a
degraded result opens a longer circuit while the durable PR fields stand.

linear_attachment_id.description:
Id of the first-class Linear attachment linking this PR on its owning
issue. `None` until the PR is first published; carried forward so later
publishes update the same attachment in place.

linear_comment_id.description:
Id of the loopflow-managed Linear comment carrying the PR URL and state.
Its presence switches the writeback from `commentCreate` to `commentUpdate`.

linear_link_error.description:
`None` when the last Linear linkage writeback succeeded; the last error
string when it degraded. The GitHub publication still succeeded — this only
records that the Linear side is behind, and is cleared on the next success.

parent_pr_id.description:
Selected parent PR, or `None` when rooted on the default branch.
Selection does not move Git: `base_commit` remains the child's last
recorded fork until sync succeeds. The link clears after the parent
merges and this PR collapses onto main.

TaskReferenceSnapshot.description:
Stable references for one Task, shared verbatim by `lf wave status` and
`lf wave show`. The issue URL is cached PM evidence. Workspace evidence comes
from the durable Task and outlives its execution and final PR.

oneOf.description: The run's Graph process registered; it goes on without its launcher.

log.description:
Where the run's output goes once its launcher lets go; null while a
terminal (`-b`, `-i`) keeps it.

run.description: The graph and where the run set out: `code from implement`.

oneOf.description: Nothing runs: the Task now waits at this interactive step.
Nothing remained: the Task is at `end`.

completion_pending.description: A durable completion request awaiting settlement.

owner.description:
Who owns the Task on which Machine, as this Machine reads the ownership
log; absent when the Task is unowned.

status.description: Completion and abandonment are independent of Graph position.

TaskSection.description:
Where a Task sits on the Wave board. The one bucketing rule: the board, the
sidebar's Working Tasks, Wave counts and `lf wave show` all read it.

oneOf.description: Waiting for someone to pick it up: unstarted, or started and unassigned.
Someone's idle, active or moving Task.
Someone's shipping Task, running to merge with nothing left for a person.

TaskSession.description: Conversation identity and completion, without loading its input or transcript.

graph_lf_process_id.description: The Graph whose step opened its current input.

oneOf.description: Auto-Ship is approved and `process` ships the Task to `end`.

log.description: The ship's output once its launcher lets go; null under `-b`.

oneOf.description: Another live process already ships it.
The Task already stands at `end`.

completion_pending.description: A durable completion request awaiting settlement.

observation.description:
Freshness of the PR state against GitHub as of this read. `Degraded`
means a bounded remote read failed and the PR fields are cached, not
freshly confirmed.

ship_approval.description: Who approved Auto-Ship and when, while the Task is approved.

ship_stop.description: The stop that keeps a run from approving Auto-Ship, until `lf ship`.

started_by.description: Who started the Task's latest Graph.

status.description: Completion and abandonment are independent of the Task's Graph position.

TaskState.description:
A Task's state, derived from its checkout, Graph position, whether a
Graph runs for it and the Auto-Ship approval. Completion and abandonment
are durable; the open states follow what the Task is doing now. Whether
anyone owns it is ownership, not state.

oneOf.description: No checkout yet.

A checkout, no Graph running and not at an interactive step: before its first run,
after a stopped one, or shipping whose ship process exited.
Between Graphs at an interactive step, in a conversation in its Task Session.
A Graph runs for it with an interactive step still ahead that will stop for a person.

A Graph runs for it and no interactive step ahead will stop it: none remain, or
Auto-Ship approved stand-ins at the rest. It finishes on its own to merge.
Completed independently of Graph position.
Its PR is open, or it finished first.
It is done or abandoned.

TaskWork.description: All retained work in a checkout, plus explicitly attributed work elsewhere.

graph.description: The graph the Task took up; `None` until its first `lf task run`.

local_exists.description: Existence on the reading Machine; unknown when the filesystem check fails.

UnavailableTaskEvidence.description:
Non-terminal durable Task Work whose historical Project is no longer in the
current PM snapshot.

Untyped.description: Untyped on the wire: any JSON value, with no shape promised.

UsageSnapshot.description: An account's windows and banked resets at one instant.

argv.description: An explicit connect command, never a fallback shell or provider launch argv.

ViewPlan.description: A passive host plan. It describes saved intent and observed Work, not native readiness.

slots.description: The page geometry visible members fill, in projection order.

Waited.description: One reading of `task.wait`: the Task now, and whether it reached the state waited for.

WaveAdded.description:
`lf wave add --json`: the receipt Desktop and the CLI both show. `summary`
holds what is left to do after the add, one sentence per line; empty when
nothing is.

WaveDetailSnapshot.description:
`lf wave status <wave>` and `lf wave plan <wave>`: current planning,
Task conditions and Session history. Wire type; no defaults.

history.description: This Wave's Machine-local Session history, newest first.

metric_portfolio.description: Wave-owned live evidence derived once by Rust for every consumer.

setup.description: What the Wave's Tasks run, where, and which logins pay, with each source.

unavailable_tasks.description:
Durable Project Work that cannot join the current PM plan, including
non-terminal Tasks stranded under a terminal historical Project.

WaveGraph.description:
The graph a scope's new Tasks take up, resolved through your `lf set wave.graph`,
the Wave's and the repository's `graph:`, then `code`.
The repository scope has no Wave.

graph.description: The graph the Wave's Tasks take up by default.

skill_agents.description: Agent by skill name, for every skill some layer names.

tasks_machine.description: Where the Wave's new Tasks run.

WaveSnapshot.description:
One wave's registry snapshot — the `lf wave list` row and the `wave` field of
`lf wave status`. Wire type consumed by Loopflow: every field is required or
explicitly Optional, no serde defaults.

active_tasks.description: Non-terminal Tasks owned by this Wave.

created_at.description: RFC3339 creation time, `null` when the row predates the column.

machine.description: Local execution placement and its route; absent for unplaced planning.

parent_wave_id.description: Parent wave id in the chord tree, `null` for a root wave.

retired_at.description: Tombstone time for stable-id history; active locator reads exclude it.

status.description: Current planning lifecycle derived from stable Work and concrete facts.

client_id.description: The server's name for this connection, as `lf server status` lists it.

machine.description: Null while the Machine registry is unavailable or uninitialized.

revision.description: The revision both sides speak for this connection.

subject.description: Current display label: Wave name, Project slug, or Task identifier.

truncated.description: More Session records exist in the window than `--limit` returned.

oneOf.description: An interrupt was recorded; `target` says what it reached and how.
Nothing was live, so nothing was recorded.

WorkLink.description: A readable, activatable Work link. Printing one opens nothing.

execution_machine.description: The execution owner when it is another Machine.

session.description: An explicit Session selection; ordinary Work links leave it absent.

task.description: The Task's readable identifier, such as LOO-507.

WorkSource.description: How this attempt received its work attribution; absent for unrecorded history.

repository.description: Durable repository plan ID, not a filesystem opening or execution locator.

oneOf.description:
`lf task create --run --json --request-id <id> -- <request>`: file a
Task from a request and start it. Runs as its own `lf` process, so the
Graph launch keeps its owner; admission survives a lost carrier reply.
`lf task create --session <id> --title <title> --json`, without launching.
`lf task complete <issue>`.
`lf task reopen <issue>`.
`lf task edit <issue> --notes=<notes>`.

`lf task abandon <issue>`: cancels the Task and removes its PRs and
branches.
`lf task claim <issue> --json`.
`lf task unassign <issue> --json`.

`lf [-b] [-a <agent>] task run <issue> [--from <step>] --json`, started
detached: the Graph process it started, or where the Task now waits.
`approve` is `-b`: every step headless to `end`, approving Auto-Ship.
`lf --task <issue> ship --json`, started detached: approves Auto-Ship.
`lf task hold <issue> --json`: withdraws the Task's Auto-Ship approval.

`lf task steer <issue> <message> --json`: direction for the Task's
runs, whoever writes it.

`lf task report <issue> <message> --json`: progress for the Task's
thread; an agent's carries its Session's provenance.
`lf task interrupt <issue> --json`.
`lf task move <issue> --wave <wave>`, or `--no-wave` without one.

`lf task save <issue> <path> --revision <revision> --json`, with
`content` on stdin.

`lf [--wave <wave>] session steer [<id>] <message> --json`: a steer
one Session, every Session of the Wave or, with neither, every Session
of the repository reads at its next boundary.
`lf session rename --json -- <id> <name>`.

actions.help: Open this Session in a terminal
actions.label: Open here

x-result-example.ready_summary: The design now reflects Jack's requested changes.
x-result-example.title: Served name

oneOf.description:
`lf session bind --json --task <task> -- <id>`; with `preview`,
`--dry-run`: the Task a bind would assign, assigning nothing.

`lf session resume --start-only --json -- <id>`: start the exact recorded
Session without a viewer, as its own `lf` process so the owner outlives
the server. Machine-scoped, like Portfolio: it runs from `/`.

`lf [--agent <agent>] session resume [<id>] [--task <task>] [--wave <wave>]
--prepare --json`, with `--repo <directory>` when it names none of them:
the conversation and the command that opens it, no provider started.

`lf [--agent <agent>] session new <id> --prepare --json`: the
conversation on a fresh provider thread, not yet started.

`lf --agent <agent> session move --all [--blocked] [--on <on>]
--json`: the open Sessions the selector names continue on the agent;
the report says which moved, which move after their turn, and which
were skipped.

`lf wave add <wave> [--objective <objective>] --json`: the Wave, its
authored files and first Project; an existing Wave is unchanged.
`lf wave sync <wave> --json`: the planning refresh.

`lf wave plan bind <wave> <project> --json`: the tracker Project
bound as the Wave's current plan.

`lf wave plan connect [<wave>|--all] [--team-key <key>]
[--team-name <name>] --json`: one receipt per Wave connected.

`lf wave plan reteam [--apply] --json`: the moves onto the
repository's Team; a plan without `apply`.

`lf graph customize <name>`: copies a builtin Graph into the repository,
recording nothing.

`lf repo release run [<version>] [-t <target>] --json`, started
detached: the Process carrying the release.
`lf [-a <agent>] commit [-m <message>] [-p] [--no-add] [<path>…] --json`.

`lf sync [<onto>] [--plan|--manual|--continue|--abort] [--adopt]
--json`: the plan, a finished continue or abort, or the Process
carrying a sync started detached.
`lf wt create <name> [--plan] [--persistent] --json`.

`lf account disconnect <provider>[=<email>]`: forget the provider's
local credentials, or one managed login's.

`lf account connect <provider>[=<email>] [--chrome-profile] [--import]
[--api-key]`. Served, no profile is chosen interactively: a login with
no remembered profile needs `chrome_profile`.

`lf account set <provider>[=<email>] …`: a managed login's lifecycle,
cooldown and browser choices, or the local credentials' browser choices.

`lf account redeem-reset <provider>=<email> [--idempotency-key]
[--credit-id] --json`: spend one banked Codex reset.

x-result-example.refresh_error: rate limits unavailable after the spend

oneOf.description: Hold one login on this Machine, or release holds with `auto`.
Pause a login's automatic rotation.
Return a login to automatic rotation.

`lf -b [--agent <agent>] graph <name> [message]`, started detached: the
Process carrying the Graph.

`lf -b [--agent <agent>] skill <name> [message]`, started detached: the
Process carrying the skill's headless run.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr publish [--title] [--body] --json`: push and
create or refresh the checkout's ready PR.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr open [--title] [--body] --json`: push and
create or refresh the checkout's draft PR; served, no review surface
opens.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr submit [--strict] [--worktree] [--message]
[--title] [--body] --json`: prepare the PR for a teammate's merge.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr arm [--strict] [--local] [--worktree]
[--message] [--title] [--body] --json`: arm exact-head auto-merge and
return.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr land [--wait-and-fix] [--strict] [--local]
[--worktree] [--message] [--title] [--body] --json`, started
detached: the Process carrying the landing.

`lf pr abandon [<branch>] [--force] --json`: close the PR and delete
its worktree and branches. Served, unpublished work is deleted only
with `force`.

`lf pr reconcile --json`: check recorded landings once and settle
verified merges.
`lf pr request-review [<pr>] -r <reviewer>… --json`.

`lf desktop portfolio <change> --json`, run from `/`: which
repositories the app shows.
`lf desktop dashboard query [--revision <revision>] -- <id> <expression>`.
`lf desktop dashboard pin <id> --revision <revision>`.
`lf desktop dashboard unpin <id> --revision <revision>`.
`lf desktop dashboard rename --revision <revision> -- query:<id> <name>`.
`lf desktop dashboard hide query:<id>/<member>`.
`lf desktop dashboard show query:<id>/<member>`.

`lf desktop dashboard slots query:<id> --revision <revision>`, with
`slots` (JSON) on stdin.

`lf desktop dashboard move <board>/<member> --destination <destination>`:
a Dashboard's tile (`query:<id>`) or the shared Task order (`working-tasks`).
`lf desktop layout <work> --save`, with `layout` (JSON) on stdin.

`lf config set <key> <value> <destination flags> --json`: declare a
setting in the destination's file; `value` is YAML.

`lf config unset <key> <destination flags> --json`: remove that
declaration so other sources choose.

Appearance's theme file at `path`: set to `value`, or read when null.
Desktop owns its Apply/Cancel transaction; no CLI spells it.
